searches.note: Twenty six searches of a share of twenty eight, none of them the author's; two left unspent. Four were restricted to a primary body's own domain and are read as primary through their summaries: arnaldocaprai.it (the history and the fiftieth year pages), cavalieridellavoro.it with quirinale.it (the honours of 2003), lungarotti.it (the Vigna Monticchio sheets) and antinori.it (the Cervaro vintage pages). The search on the Montefalco Sagrantino DOC and DOCG served Paolo Bea as well and is counted once, under Caprai. Three searches failed to find what they sought and are counted: the sector of the Cavaliere del Lavoro, a Vigna del Lago, the vineyards' height at Barberani; a fourth, for the ten years in bottle at Lungarotti, found only three to five. No WebFetch was tried. Every record was tested; no fact that rests on no source was kept in a record marked checked.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the classification and its year, the grapes, the sites, the making and its months, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, no bare family word, British spelling, no dash).

The searches went first to the bodies' own texts (the disciplinari of Montefalco Sagrantino, Torgiano, Torgiano Rosso Riserva and Orvieto, the EU's single document for Orvieto, the federation of the Cavalieri del Lavoro) and the houses' own pages for their own dates and methods, then to the press and the merchants for the second source of each date, person and place.

Where two sources disagreed on a year or a figure (the son's taking over at Caprai, the Monaldeschi marriage, the month of Cervaro's blend, Bea's months in steel) the record gives what all allow; where a detail rested on one source or none (Vigna del Lago, the sector of the honour, the decade in bottle at Lungarotti, the grandson of 1437, the winemaker of 1979, Barberani's height and December) it was cut.

Sources whose title or address names a living person, or that are a writer's own site, were read in the results and never cited: the importer most linked with Bea, named for a living person, a wine writer's own site on Bea, and a radio interview whose address names a son of Barberani.

tested: The founder and his death: Gambero Rosso, La Nazione, Il Sole 24 Ore, QdS and Doctorwine give his death at 92 at Montefalco on 4 or 5 January 2026 and his textile business; one German trade page gives January 2025 against every other, so 2026 stands. No birth year in two sources, so he carries his death alone: confirmed as written.

The Cavaliere del Lavoro: the federation's list of 2003 and the obituaries (named 2 June 2003 by President Ciampi): the year confirmed; the sector, searched on the federation's and the Quirinale's own domains, not found, so for his services to agriculture is cut.

The purchase of 1971: the house's history page and its fiftieth year article, read through search on the house's domain: land bought in 1971, the Val di Maggio estate with a few hectares already planted (four or three by page): confirmed, the added neighbouring land cut.

The son's taking over: 1986 on the house's history page, 1987 on another of its pages, 1988 in the importer's story and a merchant's profile: changed to the second half of the 1980s. The son is living and stays unnamed.

The University of Milan: the house's innovation page gives 1987 for the start of the clonal work with the university's institute of arboriculture, another source 1990; the late 1980s stands. The three clones in the national register in 2003: World of Fine Wine, with the house's research document the author cited: two sources, kept.

25 Anni: the house's wine page says it was first made with the 1993 vintage for the estate's twenty fifth anniversary, and Decanter agrees on 1993; the release of 1996 is on the importer's page: confirmed.

The making: the importer's fact sheets for 2020 and 2021 give some fifteen days of fermentation in stainless steel with indigenous yeasts, a maceration of about thirty days, 24 months in French oak barriques and at least eight months in bottle, on limestone and clay: confirmed as written. One German merchant gives 22 months and six in bottle, not tied to the vintage, and is outweighed.

The DOC and DOCG: the AIS copy of the disciplinare and the region's text give the DOC by presidential decree of 30 October 1979 and the DOCG by ministerial decree of 5 November 1992, in the types Secco and Passito: confirmed; a decree is the right word for the DOCG and the label term stands.

The sale: La Nazione and Gambero Rosso report that the Angelini group's wine arm bought a majority of the house; neither gives a date in the summaries read, so the record, which names no owner, stays as it is (see open).
Valdimaggio and Vigna del Lago: one search found no vineyard of that name; the sites clause and the third of the others are cut.

The house rules: nobody living named (the son, the professor who led the clonal work and the group's chief executive met and left out); no price, score or allocation; the hectares of the estate and of the group read and not used; no judging superlative; British; no dash. The cards and questions: one right answer each, distractors of one kind (four blends, four reasons for the name), the explanations say why the nearest wrong answer is wrong; the story question's 25 months in oak against the 24 teaches the trap.

tested: The family at Montefalco from the 1500s and the first bottling of 1980: Several importers' and merchants' pages in the results, Primal Wine, Skurnik and Mad Rose among them, agree on about 1500 (village archives in one, the land registry in another) and on 1980 as the year wine became a commercial product: confirmed as written.
The son trained as an architect who came home to the cellar, and his brother in the vines: confirmed by three sources; both living and never named.

Pagliaro's making: merchants give some 40 to 50 days on the skins (46 for one vintage), a year in steel (twelve to twenty four months in one), two years in large Slavonian oak and about a year in bottle, unfined and unfiltered with little or no sulphur: confirmed, the steel widened to a year or more.
The vineyard at about 400 metres: two merchants (about 1,300 feet; about 400 metres): confirmed.
The label: merchants print Pagliaro Secco Sagrantino di Montefalco and Montefalco Sagrantino Secco Vigna Pagliaro; Secco on the label confirmed, and the older name added to the DOCG term.
The DOC of 1979 and the DOCG of 1992 (shared with Caprai's search): the story corrected so the DOC is not given its later name.
Rosso de Véo as an Umbria Rosso IGT: a merchant's listing with the library: confirmed. Arboreus and Trebbiano Spoletino: the library's, not re-searched.

The house rules: the father, his two sons and the importer's founder met and not named; no price (a merchant's prices read and not used), no score, nothing volatile; no judging superlative; British; no dash. The cards and questions: the deposit question's distractors are four causes, the key the one the house's method gives; the story question's four years are plausible and the explanation teaches the 1500s against the 1980 bottling.

tested: Rubesco of 1962 and the first Vigna Monticchio of 1964: the house's Riserva page, Wine Industry Advisor and a merchant: confirmed.
Giorgio Lungarotti's death in 1999: Wikipedia (1910 to 1999) and the obituaries the author read; the birth year stands in Wikipedia alone, so he carries his death alone, as written.

The DOC of 1968: the AIS copy of the Torgiano disciplinare (presidential decree of 20 March 1968, amended in 1978) and the regional text (11 August 1968), with the house and two secondaries: the year confirmed.

The DOCG: the copy of the Torgiano Rosso Riserva disciplinare gives the presidential decree of 20 October 1990, published in March 1991; one secondary gives 10 October; the record's 20 October stands on the text. The rule: at least 36 months of ageing from 1 November of the harvest, 12 of them in wood and 6 in bottle, Sangiovese at least 70 per cent: the record's at least three years confirmed. The retroactive 1983 vintage: the house and a merchant.

The MUVIT and the foundation: the museum opened on 23 April 1974 (the AIS's Vitae and the house's own page), founded by the couple; the Fondazione Lungarotti in 1987: confirmed. The wife died in November 2025 aged 99 by Gambero Rosso; she stays unnamed, as before, for want of a second source for her dates.

The vineyard: the house's 2020 sheet gives the Brufa hill, about 300 metres, west south west, soils of lake origin with clay and sand in layers: confirmed. Sangiovese alone in 2020: confirmed on the same sheet.

The making and the time in bottle: the 2020 sheet (steel, 25 to 28 days on the skins, about twelve months in barriques and large casks, three years in bottle) and the release notice for the 2016 (at least three years in bottle): the making corrected and the decade of old taken out, since no source gives it.
The ageing: the 2020 sheet gives a life beyond fifty years and the house's web page an average of thirty to thirty five; the record's by the house's account stands.

The others: Rubesco Rosso di Torgiano (Falstaff, a merchant, The Hub) and San Giorgio, Umbria Rosso IGT of Cabernet Sauvignon and Sangiovese (the house's sheet, a merchant, Decanter): both notes corrected.

The house rules: the founder's two living daughters and the house's oenologist met and not named; no price, score or allocation; the vineyard's hectares on the sheet read and not used; no judging superlative (the house's own press pages of best red of Italy read and not used); British; no dash. The cards and questions: the ageing question's four regimes are of one kind and the key is the sheet's; the story question's four years are the record's four dates, each taught in the explanation.

changed.why: The house's 2020 sheet, read through search on its own domain, gives fermentation in steel at a controlled temperature with 25 to 28 days on the skins, about twelve months in fine grained barriques and casks of 50 to 55 hectolitres, then three years in bottle; the ten years of old rests on no source the refuter found: a search for it returned bottle ageing of three to five years by vintage (the 2016 at least three, the 2011 sixty months by a merchant, the 2017 over forty), and none of ten.

The first Cervaro, the 1985, Chardonnay with a small share of Grechetto: the house's pages and the author's secondary: confirmed. The house's claim of a first, put in its words.

The others: Muffato della Sala (first made 1987, picked in passes, the house's pages) and Pinot Nero della Sala (the castle's own Pinot Noir on its hillsides, the house's pages and a merchant): confirmed.

The grandson's seizure of Orvieto in 1437 and his being the first to call himself della Sala rest on one page of the estate's, a claim of a first on one source, and are cut.

tested: The founding of 1961 at Baschi above Lake Corbara: Gambero Rosso, Callmewine, Vinexus and a trade directory: confirmed. The founder: Luigi's father by Gambero Rosso and a merchant, now said; not named.
Luigi Barberani's death: 22 October 2025 by Gambero Rosso, with Doctorwine (aged 87, one source, so no birth year): confirmed.
Organic farming: the Wine Society's listing marks Calcaia organic, and merchants list it and Castagnolo as organic: confirmed.

Calcaia's making: five or six passes by hand selecting the botrytised bunches, native yeasts, temperature controlled steel, some months of maturing, the 50 cl bottle (Callmewine, xtraWine, the Wine Society): confirmed; December and the maturing in the same tanks cut.
The grapes: Grechetto and Procanico or Trebbiano Toscano on three listings; Verdello in one breakdown of the 2019 and Sauvignon Blanc in a note of the 2007: the grapes field widened.
Calcaia's first vintage: 1991 by Gambero Rosso and 1986 for the house's first Muffa Nobile by Wine with Seth; the plan's 1981 in none: left out, as the author left it.

The DOC: the presidential decree of 7 August 1971 (in the disciplinare's header, published 31 August 1971, amended 1972) and the EU's single document (C/2023/471) with the types secco, abboccato, amabile, dolce, superiore, vendemmia tardiva and muffa nobile: confirmed; Superiore's release from 1 March after the harvest is in secondaries, so the record's spring after the harvest stands without the date.
Lake Corbara: a reservoir on the Tiber behind a dam built from 1959 to 1963 (Wikipedia, the region's open data): confirmed; the vineyards' height found nowhere and cut.
Castagnolo: a dry Orvieto Classico Superiore, Grechetto led with Procanico, organic (the Wine Society, Decanter, Astor Wines, a merchant): confirmed.

The house rules: the founder's grandsons, the consultant oenologist and Luigi's widow met and not named; no price (the merchants' prices read and not used), no score (Vinous and Wine Spectator figures read and not used), nothing volatile (the hectares and bottles a year read and not used); no judging superlative (one of the known figures of Umbrian wine reworded); British; no dash. The cards and questions: the picking question's four methods are of one kind and the explanation names the passito; the founding question's years teach the DOC of 1971 against the house of 1961.
